To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new sustainable procedure for synthesis of vinyl monomers with functional groups was developed using a mixture of sulfur/selenium compounds as a functional groups donor.

the developed catalytic system is capable to selectively recognize SH/Se groups in a mixture, to form the active site of the catalyst, to tune the reaction in real time, to produce functionalized organic products, and to utilize sulfur/selenium compounds from natural and technological sources.

the developed catalytic system is able to recognize the nature of functional group in the reaction mixture and adaptively tune the reaction conditions to achieve selective synthesis of target products.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of sustainable chemistry for the efficient utilization of sulfur and selenium resources and for the production of functionalized vinyl compounds.

the development of a novel sustainable catalytic system for synthesis of functionalized monomers from a mixture of SH/SeH compounds, which can be applied to a variety of sulfur/selenium feedstocks, such as oil, technological, and natural sources of sulfur/selenides, and to a broad range of alkynes.
the development of sustainable catalytic systems that can be used to produce valuable functionalized monomers from natural resources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the catalytic system is capable to recognize the nature of the functional groups in the reaction mixture and to tune its properties in order to adapt to a dynamically changing reaction mixture.
the catalytic system is able to recognize the nature of the chalcogen atom in the mixture of sulfur/selenium compounds and adaptively incorporate them into the organic product.
the catalytic system is able to recognize SH and SeH groups and selectively incorporate them to valuable organic products via atom-economical reaction with alkynes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developed catalytic system is capable to recognize and selectively incorporate sulfur and selenium groups into organic products.

the developed approach to the adaptive recognition of SH/SeH functional groups and the ability of the catalytic system to dynamically tune itself to the reaction conditions are of great importance for further development of sustainable chemistry and catalysis.
the developed catalyst is able to adapt to the reaction environment and to recognize the most active chalcogen atoms in the mixture, which is an unprecedented ability of a catalytic system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the catalytic adaptive tuning effect can be achieved via a simple change in the metal-chalcogen interaction mode.
the adaptive catalysis can be used as a general approach to control the reaction outcome in complex reaction systems.
the adaptive tuning effect is a general phenomenon and can be used to design new efficient catalysts.
